{{Quote|If you can picture a little garbage masher on four legs and covered with fur and tusks, that's a mott. Ill-tempered and brusque, in contrast to my own sweet nature.|Lareen Dantara|<ref name="SWG:AED">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>}}
'''Motts''' were medium sized, semi-aquatic herbivores (about 1 meter at the shoulder) native to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Motts-woswfg.jpg|thumb|left|180px|An adult female and her young - one youngster chasing a [[Nuna/Legends|dwarf nuna]] for fun.]]

The motts dwelled in underground mudbank borrows. They ate a wide variety of vegetation and were a primary source of food for most swamp predators like [[Bursa/Legends|bursas]] (even Gungans occasionally killed motts). Fortunately, motts had a high reproduction rate (about 15 young per birth).<ref name=":0" />

Motts lived in communes of up to 15 adults. Communes usually consisted of a dominant male and, perhaps, one lieutenant male that guarded the females and young.<ref name=":0" />

Threat displays to determine dominance was exhibited by both sexes.<ref name=":0">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

They were very good swimmers, and young often hitched rides on an adult's back. They also had good hearing and a nose horn for rooting out food.<ref name=":0" /> [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] found motts to be good pets even though motts were known for tearing up flower gardens.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Mott4-woswfg.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Swimming motts.]]

The mott can be spotted during the swamp stampede sequence of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|Episode I]], as well as the arrival at the [[Gungan Sacred Place/Legends|Gungan Sacred Place]] later in the film. In both cases, the creature is realized as a computer generated creation.<ref name="DB">{{DB|creature|mott|mott}}</ref>
